claim: At the Arabidopsis floral repressor FLOWERING LOCUS C (FLC), 'digital' Polycomb silencing facilitates quantitative epigenetic memory in response to cold.
source: At the Arabidopsis floral repressor FLOWERING LOCUS C (FLC), 'digital' Polycomb silencing is known to facilitate quantitative epigenetic memory in response to cold.
evidence: This is stated as known in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: FLC expression before cold is regulated by both analog and digital modes.
source: Using quantitative fluorescent imaging of FLC mRNA and protein, together with mathematical modeling, we find that FLC expression before cold is regulated by both analog and digital modes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data and modeling.

claim: There is a temporal separation between analog and digital modes of FLC regulation, with analog preceding digital.
source: We observe a temporal separation between the two modes, with analog preceding digital.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The analog mode can maintain intermediate expression levels at individual FLC gene copies before subsequent digital silencing.
source: The analog mode can maintain intermediate expression levels at individual FLC gene copies, before subsequent digital silencing, consistent with the copies switching OFF stochastically and heritably without cold.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental observations.

claim: FLC gene copies switch OFF stochastically and heritably without cold.
source: The analog mode can maintain intermediate expression levels at individual FLC gene copies, before subsequent digital silencing, consistent with the copies switching OFF stochastically and heritably without cold.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing digital switching patterns.

claim: Digital switching of FLC leads to a slow reduction in FLC expression at the cell population level.
source: This switch leads to a slow reduction in FLC expression at the cell population level.
evidence: This is observed in the timeseries experiments.

claim: Individual FLC gene copies make a cis-mediated, digital switch from an 'ON' (expressing) state to an 'OFF' (silenced) state during cold.
source: This quantitative response is achieved through individual FLC gene copies making a cis-mediated, digital switch from an 'ON' (expressing) state to an 'OFF' (silenced) state (Angel et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Angel et al., 2011.

claim: The digital switch of FLC during cold is asynchronous between gene copies, even in the same cell.
source: This switch is asynchronous between gene copies, even in the same cell, with the number switched OFF increasing over time in the cold.
evidence: This is stated as a known property of FLC regulation during cold.

claim: Silenced FLC gene copies are covered by high levels of the silencing histone mark H3K27me3 controlled by Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2).
source: This results in a gradual decrease in FLC expression over time at a whole plant level with silenced gene copies covered by high levels of the silencing histone mark H3K27me3 controlled by the Polycomb system through Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about FLC silencing.

claim: FLC represses the transition to flowering.
source: FLC represses the transition to flowering and is controlled by FRIGIDA, the autonomous pathway and the vernalization pathway (inducing digital epigenetic silencing in the cold).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and stated in the text.

claim: FLC is controlled by FRIGIDA, the autonomous pathway, and the vernalization pathway.
source: FLC represses the transition to flowering and is controlled by FRIGIDA, the autonomous pathway and the vernalization pathway (inducing digital epigenetic silencing in the cold).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1B and is established knowledge.

claim: Reduced FCA activity leads to higher cell population-level FLC expression in fca mutants.
source: Reduced FCA activity leads to higher cell population-level FLC expression in fca mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C with qPCR data.

claim: Wildtype Ler has the lowest FLC expression among Ler, fca-3, and fca-1.
source: Wildtype Ler has lowest FLC expression, fca-3 intermediate and fca-1 highest.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C with qPCR measurements.

claim: fca-3 has intermediate FLC expression between Ler and fca-1.
source: Wildtype Ler has lowest FLC expression, fca-3 intermediate and fca-1 highest.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C with qPCR measurements.

claim: fca-1 has the highest FLC expression among Ler, fca-3, and fca-1.
source: Wildtype Ler has lowest FLC expression, fca-3 intermediate and fca-1 highest.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C with qPCR measurements.

claim: The mean number of FLC mRNA transcripts per cell is highest in fca-1, lowest in Ler, and intermediate in fca-3.
source: We observed that the mean number of FLC mRNA transcripts per cell was highest in fca-1, lowest in Ler, and intermediate in fca-3, with the distributions being significantly different (Figure 2C, all differences significant with Bonferroni-adjusted p≤1.2 · 10-9)
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2C with smFISH data and statistical analysis.

claim: 89% of fca-1 cells have higher FLC expression than the 95th percentile of fca-3 cells.
source: with 89% of fca-1 cells having higher expression than the 95th percentile of fca-3 cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the smFISH data.

claim: In ON cells, the mRNA numbers in fca-3 are only around 1/5 of those in fca-1.
source: Furthermore, when looking only at the ON cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C; ON cells defined here as cells with more than three mRNAs counted, though the conclusion is unchanged with alternative thresholds; Figure 2—figure supplement 2), the mRNA numbers in fca-3 were only around 1/5 of those in fca-1, much less than one-half, ruling out that the reduced levels in fca-3 were solely due to silencing of one of the two gene copies.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the smFISH data for ON cells.

claim: The reduced FLC levels in fca-3 are not solely due to silencing of one of the two gene copies.
source: the mRNA numbers in fca-3 were only around 1/5 of those in fca-1, much less than one-half, ruling out that the reduced levels in fca-3 were solely due to silencing of one of the two gene copies.
evidence: This is inferred from the quantitative comparison of mRNA levels.

claim: 72% of fca-3 cells are apparently silenced (digitally OFF) with three or fewer mRNAs counted.
source: Firstly, there were different fractions of apparently silenced cells (digitally OFF) without any appreciable expression (three or fewer mRNAs counted): 72% in fca-3 and 1.5% in fca-1.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the smFISH data.

claim: 1.5% of fca-1 cells are apparently silenced (digitally OFF) with three or fewer mRNAs counted.
source: Firstly, there were different fractions of apparently silenced cells (digitally OFF) without any appreciable expression (three or fewer mRNAs counted): 72% in fca-3 and 1.5% in fca-1.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the smFISH data.

claim: In cells that express FLC (digitally ON), the FCA mutations lead to an analog change in their expression levels.
source: Secondly, in cells that did express FLC (digitally ON), the FCA mutations lead to an analog change in their expression levels, so that there was more FLC mRNA in fca-1 ON cells than in the fca-3 ON cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of mRNA levels in ON cells.

claim: FLC-Venus mRNA has a half-life of approximately 5 hours in fca-1.
source: We found that both degradation rates were quite fast, with half-lives of ~5 and ~1.5 hr, respectively, for the mRNA and protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is measured experimentally using actinomycin D treatment.

claim: FLC-Venus protein has a half-life of approximately 1.5 hours in fca-1.
source: We found that both degradation rates were quite fast, with half-lives of ~5 and ~1.5 hr, respectively, for the mRNA and protein (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is measured experimentally using cycloheximide treatment.

claim: The half-lives of FLC mRNA and protein are short compared to the cell cycle duration of approximately 1 day.
source: These timescales are short compared to the cell cycle duration, here of ~1 d (Rahni and Birnbaum, 2019), let alone compared to the timescale of development.
evidence: This is a comparison of measured half-lives to literature values for cell cycle duration.

claim: Slow degradation is unlikely to be the cause of the apparent analog regulation and observed heritability in root images.
source: Therefore, slow degradation is unlikely to be the cause of the apparent analog regulation and of the observed heritability seen in our root images.
evidence: This is inferred from the short half-lives measured.

claim: FLC expression decreases over time in fca-3 and Ler between 7 and 21 days after sowing.
source: This experiment revealed a decreasing trend in fca-3 and Ler (Figure 3A), which did not seem to be due to a change in FCA expression over the same timescale (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is shown in the timeseries qPCR data in Figure 3A.

claim: The decrease in FLC expression over time in fca-3 and Ler is not due to a change in FCA expression.
source: This experiment revealed a decreasing trend in fca-3 and Ler (Figure 3A), which did not seem to be due to a change in FCA expression over the same timescale (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is inferred from comparing FLC and FCA expression timeseries in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: The most likely explanation for the FLC decrease over time is primarily one-way switching from a heritable FLC ON state to a heritable silenced OFF state occurring digitally and independently at individual loci in fca-3 and Ler.
source: We therefore concluded that the most likely explanation was primarily one-way switching from an otherwise heritable FLC ON state, to the heritable silenced OFF state occurring digitally and independently at individual loci in fca-3 and Ler.
evidence: This is inferred from the timeseries data and the lack of FCA expression changes.

claim: The fraction of ON cells decreases over time in fca-3 roots.
source: By imaging FLC-Venus, we observed that the fraction of ON cells was indeed decreasing in fca-3, over the time course (Figure 3C and D, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is shown in the confocal imaging timeseries data.

claim: After 21 days, the pattern of ON/OFF cells in fca-3 roots is very similar to that of plants that had experienced cold leading to partial cell population-level FLC shutdown.
source: In fact, after 21 d the pattern of ON/OFF cells in the fca-3 roots was very similar to that of plants that had experienced cold leading to partial cell population-level FLC shutdown, with the majority of cell files being stably repressed, but still with some long files of cells in which FLC was ON (compare timepoint 21 in Figure 3C and figures in Berry et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison of imaging data to previously published results.

claim: The change over time in fca-3 is not due to an analog change in the expression of the ON cells but rather a decreasing number of ON cells.
source: We also examined whether the change over time in fca-3 could be due to an analog change in the expression of the ON cells rather than a decreasing number of ON cells. By setting a threshold at an intensity of 1, we look at only the tail of the ON cell distribution (normalized by the total number of these cells in each condition) (Figure 3—figure supplement 4). We see that high-intensity cells are still present at later times and do not show a reduction in intensity relative to earlier timepoints. This finding is consistent with digital regulation: a decrease in the number of ON cells, but with all remaining ON cells expressing FLC at similarly high levels over time.
evidence: This is inferred from analysis of the ON cell distribution over time.

claim: The mathematical model incorporating digital switching can recapitulate the FLC distribution over time in fca-3.
source: With these assumptions, our model could be fit ('Materials and methods') to replicate the observed pattern of increasing OFF cells in fca-3 roots, as well as the quantitative histograms for protein levels in fca-3 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is shown by comparing model output to experimental data in Figure 4B.

claim: The best fit model has an OFF-to-ON rate that is over 10 times slower than the ON-to-OFF rate.
source: In terms of the switching, we found the best fit where the OFF-to-ON rate is over 10 times slower than the ON-to-OFF rate (Figure 4B, Supplementary file 1), supporting predominantly one-way switching from an analog into a digitally silenced state.
evidence: This is determined from model fitting to experimental data.

claim: The model supports predominantly one-way switching from an analog state into a digitally silenced state.
source: In terms of the switching, we found the best fit where the OFF-to-ON rate is over 10 times slower than the ON-to-OFF rate (Figure 4B, Supplementary file 1), supporting predominantly one-way switching from an analog into a digitally silenced state.
evidence: This is inferred from the model fitting results.

claim: Analog regulation at FLC arises through the autonomous pathway, as illustrated by the fca mutants, before digital switching into a heritable silenced state.
source: In this work, we have uncovered a combination of analog and digital transcriptional regulation for the gene FLC: analog regulation arises through the autonomous pathway, as illustrated by the fca mutants, before digital switching into a heritable silenced state.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data and modeling.

claim: The silenced state at FLC is Polycomb dependent.
source: The silenced state is Polycomb dependent, given the similarity of our data to the vernalized state and the role of the Polycomb mark H3K27me3 in silencing FLC in wildtype Ler and Col-0 in the absence of cold treatment.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison to known vernalized states and literature on H3K27me3.

claim: The rate of digital Polycomb silencing is dependent on the transcription levels.
source: Based on previous studies on the interplay between transcription and PRC2 silencing (Beltran et al., 2016; Berry et al., 2017; Holoch et al., 2021; Lövkvist et al., 2021), we propose that the rate of digital Polycomb silencing is dependent on the transcription levels.
evidence: This is proposed based on previous studies cited.

claim: Transcription levels at FLC are genetically controlled and constitute analog regulation.
source: These transcription levels are genetically controlled and constitute analog regulation since the pathways governing this process are capable of graded expression control.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of graded expression in different genotypes.

claim: In Ler, low analog transcription is not sufficient to significantly oppose silencing and so the switch occurs before 7 days after sowing.
source: In the case of Ler, low analog transcription is not sufficient to significantly oppose silencing and so the switch occurs before our first experimental measurements at 7 d.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ler is mostly OFF at 7 days.

claim: In fca-1, the digital switch does not occur, prevented by high analog transcription.
source: In fca-1, the switch does not occur at all, prevented by high analog transcription in that genotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that fca-1 remains ON over time.

claim: For fca-3, with intermediate analog FLC expression, the digital switching occurs slowly and can be observed in timeseries experiments.
source: However, for fca-3, with intermediate analog FLC expression, the digital switching occurs slowly and so can be observed in our timeseries experiments, underlining a clear temporal separation of analog and digital transcriptional control.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the timeseries experimental data.

claim: The timescale for switching between analog and digital states is controlled by the strength of initial analog transcription.
source: In this way, both analog and digital regulation are combined at FLC, with the timescale for switching between these states controlled by the strength of initial analog transcription.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing the different genotypes.

claim: Switching to the OFF state in fca-3 causes a gradual reduction in FLC expression at the whole plant level.
source: In fca-3, such switching to the OFF state causes a gradual reduction in FLC expression at the whole plant level.
evidence: This is observed in the qPCR timeseries data.

claim: Images of roots at 21 days after sowing without cold are visually strikingly like images of vernalized roots.
source: Moreover, images of roots at 21 d after sowing without cold, with fluorescently labeled FLC, are visually strikingly like images of vernalized roots, where in both cases we find whole files of either all ON or all OFF cells.
evidence: This is a qualitative comparison of imaging data.

claim: The molecular characteristics of the Polycomb silenced state at FLC generated either with or without cold treatment are similar.
source: These comparisons suggest similarities in the molecular characteristics of the Polycomb silenced state at FLC generated either with or without cold treatment.
evidence: This is inferred from the visual similarity of imaging data.

claim: In the absence of active Polycomb, the fca alleles would display only analog differences, without the possibility of digital silencing.
source: We hypothesize that in the absence of active Polycomb the fca alleles would display only analog differences, without the possibility of digital silencing.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the proposed mechanism.

claim: The endogenous Ler FLC carries a Mutator transposable element (TE) in intron 1, silencing FLC expression.
source: The endogenous Ler FLC carries a Mutator transposable element (TE) in intron 1, silencing FLC expression (Liu et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as known from the literature.

claim: FLC mRNA accumulates in the nucleolus in the Ler background, possibly because of the transposable element.
source: Possibly because of the TE, we observed FLC mRNA accumulation in the nucleolus in this background (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is observed in smFISH images and speculated to be due to the TE.

claim: Comparison of whole-plant gene expression showed similar behavior in the mutants for both the endogenous and transformed FLC.
source: Comparison of whole-plant gene expression showed similar behavior in the mutants for both the endogenous and transformed FLC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is shown in qPCR data comparing endogenous and transgenic FLC.

claim: Short files of ON cells can be observed in fca-3.
source: Furthermore, we could see a mix of distinct ON and OFF cells by enhancing the fca-3 images to increase the Venus intensity to a similar level as in fca-1. By contrast, in fca-1 all cells were ON, whereas in Ler, cells appeared OFF even with an equivalent adjustment (Figure 2D(iv), Figure 2—figure supplement 3). We could also infer a potentially heritable component in the ON/OFF states as short files of ON cells could be observed in fca-3 (Figure 2D(v), Figure 2—figure supplement 3, yellow boxes).
evidence: This is observed in confocal imaging data.

claim: Short ON files are also observed in fca-4, suggesting this is a general feature not specific to fca-3.
source: In fca-4, we observed similar short ON files (Figure 2—figure supplement 3, yellow boxes), suggesting that this is a general feature that is not specific to fca-3.
evidence: This is observed in confocal imaging data for fca-4.

claim: In Ler most cells are digitally OFF.
source: Overall, our results support a combination of analog and digital regulation for FLC: in Ler most cells were digitally OFF, in fca-1 all cells were digitally ON, while in fca-3 a fraction of cells were OFF, but for those cells that were ON, the level of FLC expression was reduced in an analog way relative to fca-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the smFISH and imaging data.

claim: In fca-1 all cells are digitally ON.
source: Overall, our results support a combination of analog and digital regulation for FLC: in Ler most cells were digitally OFF, in fca-1 all cells were digitally ON, while in fca-3 a fraction of cells were OFF, but for those cells that were ON, the level of FLC expression was reduced in an analog way relative to fca-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the smFISH and imaging data.

claim: In fca-3 a fraction of cells are OFF, but for those cells that are ON, the level of FLC expression is reduced in an analog way relative to fca-1.
source: Overall, our results support a combination of analog and digital regulation for FLC: in Ler most cells were digitally OFF, in fca-1 all cells were digitally ON, while in fca-3 a fraction of cells were OFF, but for those cells that were ON, the level of FLC expression was reduced in an analog way relative to fca-1.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the smFISH and imaging data.

claim: FLC mRNA has previously been shown to have a half-life of approximately 6 hours in ColFRI.
source: FLC mRNA has previously been shown to have a half-life of approximately 6 hr (Ietswaart et al., 2017) in a different genotype (ColFRI) to that used here.
evidence: This is cited from previous literature.

claim: FLC expression is similar in roots and leaves, suggesting that each mutation has similar effects in different tissues.
source: We found similar protein expression patterns in roots and leaves, suggesting that each mutation was having similar effects in different tissues.
evidence: This is observed by comparing imaging data from roots and leaves.

claim: The commonly used Arabidopsis accessions Ler and Col-0 have mutations in the FRI gene.
source: The commonly used Arabidopsis accessions Ler and Col-0, have mutations in the FRI gene, allowing the autonomous pathway to dominate, thereby repressing FLC during vegetative development and resulting in a rapidly cycling summer annual lifestyle (Johanson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as known from the literature.

claim: Mutations in FRI in Ler and Col-0 allow the autonomous pathway to dominate, thereby repressing FLC during vegetative development.
source: The commonly used Arabidopsis accessions Ler and Col-0, have mutations in the FRI gene, allowing the autonomous pathway to dominate, thereby repressing FLC during vegetative development and resulting in a rapidly cycling summer annual lifestyle (Johanson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as known from the literature.

claim: Genetic introduction of an active FRI allele (ColFRI) generates an initially high FLC expression state.
source: On the other hand, genetic introduction of an active FRI allele (ColFRI, Lee and Amasino, 1995) generates an initially high FLC expression state, which then requires cold for FLC repression and subsequent flowering.
evidence: This is stated as known from the literature.

claim: ColFRI requires cold for FLC repression and subsequent flowering.
source: On the other hand, genetic introduction of an active FRI allele (ColFRI, Lee and Amasino, 1995) generates an initially high FLC expression state, which then requires cold for FLC repression and subsequent flowering.
evidence: This is stated as known from the literature.

claim: fca-1 is a complete loss of function mutant.
source: One of these mutants, fca-1 (Koornneef et al., 1991), is a complete loss of function and therefore exhibits late flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and high FLC expression before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D), similar to ColFRI.
evidence: This is stated based on literature and experimental data.

claim: fca-1 exhibits late flowering.
source: One of these mutants, fca-1 (Koornneef et al., 1991), is a complete loss of function and therefore exhibits late flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and high FLC expression before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D), similar to ColFRI.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: fca-1 exhibits high FLC expression before cold, similar to ColFRI.
source: One of these mutants, fca-1 (Koornneef et al., 1991), is a complete loss of function and therefore exhibits late flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) and high FLC expression before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D), similar to ColFRI.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Wildtype Ler has a fully functional autonomous pathway.
source: The wildtype, Ler, has a fully functional autonomous pathway and so exhibits low FLC levels before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and early flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), with the FLC gene covered by the silencing histone mark H3K27me3 (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as known.

claim: Wildtype Ler exhibits low FLC levels before cold.
source: The wildtype, Ler, has a fully functional autonomous pathway and so exhibits low FLC levels before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and early flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), with the FLC gene covered by the silencing histone mark H3K27me3 (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Wildtype Ler exhibits early flowering.
source: The wildtype, Ler, has a fully functional autonomous pathway and so exhibits low FLC levels before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and early flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), with the FLC gene covered by the silencing histone mark H3K27me3 (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In wildtype Ler, the FLC gene is covered by the silencing histone mark H3K27me3.
source: The wildtype, Ler, has a fully functional autonomous pathway and so exhibits low FLC levels before cold (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and early flowering (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), with the FLC gene covered by the silencing histone mark H3K27me3 (Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is cited from Wu et al., 2020.

claim: fca-3 and fca-4 mutants lead to compromised FCA function.
source: Crucially, however, the fca-3 and fca-4 mutants lead to compromised FCA function (see 'Materials and methods' and Koornneef et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated based on literature and materials and methods.

claim: In fca-3, there is a splice site mutation that leads to changed exon structure through variable use of alternative splice sites with either loss or misfolding of the C-terminus.
source: In fca-3, there is a splice site mutation that leads to changed exon structure through variable use of alternative splice sites with either loss or misfolding of the C-terminus (Macknight et al., 2002).
evidence: This is cited from Macknight et al., 2002.

claim: The fca-4 allele is the result of a large genomic inversion that disrupts the FCA gene at the 3′ end of exon 4.
source: The fca-4 allele is the result of a large genomic inversion that disrupts the FCA gene at the 3′ end of exon 4 (Page et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Page et al., 1999.

claim: The expressed 3′ fragment in fca-4 contains the second RNA-binding domain and the C-terminal region of the protein including the WW protein interaction domain, sufficient to give an intermediate flowering time phenotype.
source: The expressed 3′ fragment contains the second RNA-binding domain and the C-terminal region of the protein including the WW protein interaction domain, sufficient to give an intermediate flowering time phenotype (Page et al., 1999).
evidence: This is cited from Page et al., 1999.

claim: fca-3 and fca-4 display intermediate cell population-level FLC expression.
source: Both mutants display intermediate cell population-level FLC expression (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and flowering time (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), indicating partial functionality of the FCA protein in these mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: fca-3 and fca-4 display intermediate flowering time.
source: Both mutants display intermediate cell population-level FLC expression (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and flowering time (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), indicating partial functionality of the FCA protein in these mutants.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The intermediate FLC expression and flowering time in fca-3 and fca-4 indicate partial functionality of the FCA protein in these mutants.
source: Both mutants display intermediate cell population-level FLC expression (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–D) and flowering time (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), indicating partial functionality of the FCA protein in these mutants.
evidence: This is inferred from the intermediate phenotypes.

claim: FLC levels are set during embryogenesis by competition between FRIGIDA and the autonomous repressive pathway.
source: FLC levels are set during embryogenesis by competition between an FLC activator called FRIGIDA (FRI) and the so-called autonomous repressive pathway (Figure 1B, Li et al., 2018; Schon et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from Li et al., 2018 and Schon et al., 2021.

claim: FRIGIDA is an FLC activator.
source: FLC levels are set during embryogenesis by competition between an FLC activator called FRIGIDA (FRI) and the so-called autonomous repressive pathway (Figure 1B, Li et al., 2018; Schon et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as known.

claim: The autonomous pathway is a repressive pathway for FLC.
source: FLC levels are set during embryogenesis by competition between an FLC activator called FRIGIDA (FRI) and the so-called autonomous repressive pathway (Figure 1B, Li et al., 2018; Schon et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as known.

claim: FCA is part of the FLC-repressive autonomous pathway.
source: In this work, we exploited mutant alleles in FLOWERING CONTROL LOCUS A (FCA), which is part of the FLC-repressive autonomous pathway, thereby systematically varying overall FLC levels.
evidence: This is stated as known.

claim: The model can capture the longer files present in the later timepoints in the data.
source: In addition, the model could capture the longer files present in the later timepoints in the data (T21, Figure 3C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1), but unlike in the data these were not more prevalent at later timepoints than earlier.
evidence: This is a comparison of model output to experimental data.

claim: The altered prevalence of longer files at later timepoints in the data may suggest additional developmental influence on the heritability of the ON/OFF state at later times in the plant.
source: Therefore, the altered prevalence of this effect in the data may suggest additional developmental influence on the heritability of the ON/OFF state at later times in the plant.
evidence: This is inferred from the difference between model and data.

claim: The main antagonist of the autonomous pathway is the FRIGIDA gene.
source: The main antagonist of the autonomous pathway is the FRIGIDA gene, a transcriptional activator of FLC (Figure 1B), which was not present in the lines used in this study.
evidence: This is stated as known.

claim: FRIGIDA is a transcriptional activator of FLC.
source: The main antagonist of the autonomous pathway is the FRIGIDA gene, a transcriptional activator of FLC (Figure 1B), which was not present in the lines used in this study.
evidence: This is stated as known.

claim: It is the antagonism between FRI and the autonomous pathway that determines the starting FLC levels.
source: In fact, it is the antagonism between FRI and the autonomous pathway that determines the starting FLC levels, and so we would expect that FRI controls the analog component directly and digital component indirectly.
evidence: This is inferred from the known roles of FRI and the autonomous pathway.

claim: FRI controls the analog component directly and digital component indirectly.
source: In fact, it is the antagonism between FRI and the autonomous pathway that determines the starting FLC levels, and so we would expect that FRI controls the analog component directly and digital component indirectly.
evidence: This is inferred from the proposed mechanism.

claim: Natural accessions show mutations in FRI rather than in autonomous pathway components, possibly because the autonomous components regulate many more target genes.
source: This could be particularly important because natural accessions show mutations in FRI rather than in autonomous pathway components, possibly because the autonomous components regulate many more target genes.
evidence: This is stated with speculation about the reason.

claim: The analog component of transcriptional regulation at FLC could have widespread ecological relevance.
source: The analog component of transcriptional regulation could therefore have widespread ecological relevance.
evidence: This is speculated based on the findings.

claim: The high FLC genotype Lov-1 has higher FLC expression upon germination in early autumn compared to ColFRI.
source: For example, the high FLC genotype Lov-1, a natural accession from Sweden, has higher FLC expression upon germination in early autumn compared to ColFRI (Coustham et al., 2012).
evidence: This is cited from Coustham et al., 2012.

claim: The analog component could be dominating in Lov-1, with all cells having a higher ON level.
source: The analog component could be dominating in Lov-1, with all cells having a higher ON level.
evidence: This is speculated based on the findings.

claim: Lov-1 has lower levels of the Polycomb mark H3K27me3 at the FLC locus, with potentially few or no OFF cells in the warm.
source: Consistent with this, Lov-1 also has lower levels of the Polycomb mark H3K27me3 at the FLC locus, with potentially few or no OFF cellsn the warm (Qüesta et al., 2020).

claim: It is the strength of the initial analog, autonomous pathway transcriptional level that controls the timescale for the switch into the subsequent digital, Polycomb silenced state.
source: We further propose it is the strength of the initial analog, autonomous pathway transcriptional level that controls the timescale for the switch into the subsequent digital, Polycomb silenced state.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study.

claim: In Col-0, in a mutant of the PRC2 component and H3K27 methyltransferase clf, FLC is upregulated and H3K27me3 reduced.
source: In Col-0, in a mutant of the PRC2 component and H3K27 methyltransferase, clf, it has also been observed that FLC is upregulated and H3K27me3 reduced (Shu et al., 2019), though this is only a partial effect due to the presence of an active SWN, another PRC2 H3K27 methyltransferase.
evidence: This is cited from Shu et al., 2019.
